title: RemoteRunnerMessageV1
description: ADR-0006 thin protocol between the single control plane (CrossMini) and the lap runner daemon over Tailscale. Only the control plane initiates HTTP requests (dispatch, status, result, cancel, health); the runner never calls back. Dispatch carries a cmap1 dispatch permit bound to runner_id, adapter audience and the exact envelope SHA256; the runner verifies it with a pinned public key and at most 2 seconds of clock skew. Input files are frozen by the control plane and shipped inline; result artifacts are pulled by the control plane, which recomputes every SHA256 itself and never trusts runner-reported hashes. Bodies never carry credentials, database addresses or provider stderr; error bodies carry only category, code and retryable. Application-layer authentication (ADR-0006 Stage 3): every request, health included, carries requestAuthHeaders signed by the control plane permit key (Ed25519) over method, path+query, body sha256, millisecond timestamp (skew at most 2 seconds), nonce (single use inside the window) and audience runner_id; any failure is an identical unsigned 401 error with code UNAUTHORIZED and no detail, and nothing is executed. Every other response carries responseAuthHeaders signed by the runner key over audience, the request nonce, status and body sha256; the control plane pins the runner public key and treats a bad signature like an evidence hash mismatch.

requestAuthHeaders.title: RemoteRunnerRequestAuthHeadersV1
requestAuthHeaders.description: HTTP headers on every control-plane request. Signature (base64url Ed25519, 64 bytes) covers the UTF-8 string 'cmap-runner-req1' LF METHOD LF path+query LF x-cmap-content-sha256 LF x-cmap-timestamp LF x-cmap-nonce LF x-cmap-audience. x-cmap-content-sha256 is the sha256 of the exact body bytes (empty body included); x-cmap-audience must equal the runner's own runner_id.

responseAuthHeaders.title: RemoteRunnerResponseAuthHeadersV1
responseAuthHeaders.description: HTTP header on every authenticated runner response (errors and 204 included; the 401 for failed request authentication is the only unsigned reply). Signature (base64url Ed25519 by the runner key) covers the UTF-8 string 'cmap-runner-res1' LF audience runner_id LF request x-cmap-nonce LF status code LF sha256 of the exact body bytes.

dispatch.title: RemoteRunnerDispatchV1
dispatch.description: POST /v1/tasks. envelope is the exact control-plane TaskEnvelopeV1; its integrity comes from permit.envelope_sha256, not from this schema.

uri.description: 控制面已冻结的输入：memory/review 快照、continues 续作输入或 DAG 父节点产物（inputs/<node_id>/<桶>/payload）；第二段为 safe_id，不含点与斜杠。

dispatchAccepted.title: RemoteRunnerDispatchAcceptedV1
dispatchAccepted.description: Response to dispatch. A replay of the same permit to the same runner returns the existing remote_task_id without a second execution.

status.title: RemoteRunnerStatusV1
status.description: Response to GET /v1/tasks/{remote_task_id}. No provider detail or stderr crosses the wire.

result.title: RemoteRunnerResultV1
result.description: Response to GET /v1/tasks/{remote_task_id}/result. result must validate as TaskResultV1 on the control plane; identity fields are overwritten by the control plane. Each artifact is pulled inline and its sha256 is recomputed by the control plane before any ledger write.

cancel.title: RemoteRunnerCancelV1
cancel.description: POST /v1/tasks/{remote_task_id}/cancel. reason is a control-plane code, never prompt text.

health.title: RemoteRunnerHealthV1
health.description: Response to GET /v1/health. The control plane probes with a 3 second timeout before routing; anything but healthy falls back to local candidates. admission publishes the runner's own allowlist (the same RUNNER_ALLOWED_* / RUNNER_MAX_RISK it enforces at dispatch) so the control plane can skip the runner before dispatch when tenant, owner, capability or risk would be denied, and fall back to local candidates instead of collecting an admission denial. It is advisory for routing only: the runner still enforces admission on every dispatch (defence in depth). It is signed with the rest of the response; a health reply without it is invalid and the runner is treated as unavailable.

admission.title: RemoteRunnerAdmissionV1
admission.description: The runner's dispatch allowlist, same semantics as runner-admission.v1: explicit empty lists deny all.

error.title: RemoteRunnerErrorV1
error.description: permit: DispatchPermitErrorCode, no execution happened. admission: RunnerAdmissionErrorCode from the runner's own allowlist, no execution happened. adapter: AdapterError code from the wrapped adapter. protocol: malformed request, unknown task or oversized body, or UNAUTHORIZED (HTTP 401, unsigned, identical for every authentication failure).
